title: A Novel Method for Reducing Charging in SEM by Simultaneous Irradiation with an Electron Beam and VUV Light
content: Scanning electron microscopes (SEMs) are widely used to observe small features. However, samples for SEM typically need to have conductivity because SEM uses an electron beam (EB) as a probe. There are various methods to reduce charging on nonconductive samples in SEM, but current methods can also have negative side effects. Conductive coating of a sample may obscure the surface details, and using low vacuum (LV) mode may reduce the S/N ratio significantly and produce an indistinct image due to the scattering of the electrons in the chamber. It is already known that a vacuum ultra-violet (VUV) light can reduce electrostatic charging issues [1-3] and has been applied to the semiconductor and polymer fields [4]. In this study, a VUV light has been applied to reduce charging in SEM imaging.
